data.title: Malaysia Auto Sales Could Pick Up in November on Year-End Promotions — Market Talk
data.description: Malaysia's auto sales in November could be sequentially stronger, driven by more aggressive year-end discounting and festive promotions, Affin Hwang IB analyst Afifah Ishak says in a note. Automakers are expected to step up efforts to boost deliveries ahead of the year-end, she says. The analyst maintains her 2026 Malaysia auto sales estimate at 815,000 units, down 1% from a year earlier. Affin Hwang maintains a neutral rating on the Malaysian auto and auto-parts sector, pegging MBM Resources as its top pick, citing its resilient earnings profile, underpinned by its associate stake in national carmaker Perodua. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)

data.title: Australian shares recover from June low as miners rally
data.description:
Australian shares clawed back from a 5-1/2-month low on Monday, led by a rebound in battered mining and gold stocks, although losses in banks and economic slowdown concerns kept a lid on gains.

The S&P/ASX 200 index rose 0.1% to 8,600.1 by 0042 GMT after falling as much as 0.8% earlier in the session to its lowest level since June 9. The benchmark had declined 1.6% on Friday.

Mining stocks climbed 1.3%, recovering after the sub-index hit an eight-month low on Friday and shed more than 15% over the previous seven sessions. Heavyweights BHP and Rio Tinto gained 2% and 0.4%, respectively.

Gold miners rose 1.4%, snapping an eight-session losing streak after bullion prices jumped more than 1%. Evolution Mining advanced 2.7%.

However, a 0.6% decline in financials limited the broader market's gains. The sector was on track for a fifth straight day of losses, with the country's big four banks down between 0.3% and 1.4%.

Last week's soft jobs data pointed to easing labour market tightness and largely ruled out chances of further interest-rate hikes while stoking concerns about a possible economic slowdown.

Swaps now imply a 92.6% chance that the Reserve Bank of Australia will hold the cash rate steady next month, with rate cuts largely expected only from mid-2027.

Attention now turns to the October inflation report, due on Wednesday, for further clues on the central bank's policy outlook.

Technology stocks slipped 0.1%, tracking losses in Wall Street peers following an AI-driven selloff. Sector heavyweights Xero and WiseTech Global fell 1% and 0.3%, respectively.

Energy stocks fell 0.7%, tracking a decline in oil prices, with sector leaders Woodside Energy down 1.4% and Santos losing 0.3%.

Across the Tasman Sea, New Zealand's benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index fell 1.1% to 13,948, the lowest in about two weeks.

data.title: Steady Start Eyes For China Stock Market
data.description:
BEIJING (dpa-AFX) - The China stock market has moved lower in two straight sessions, sliding more than 50 points or 1.4 percent along the way. The Shanghai Composite Index now sits just above the 3,530-point plateau although it may find traction on Monday.

The global forecast for the Asian markets suggests volatility after last week's heavy selling, with technology shares likely to see continued selling pressure. The European and U.S. markets were sharply lower and the oversold Asian bourses are expected to at least open in the red.

The SCI finished sharply lower on Monday following losses from the technology, semiconductor, industrial, retail and mineral sectors.

For the day, the index slumped 43.83 points or 1.23 percent to finish at 3,533.79 after trading between 3,500.83 and 3,538.27. The Shenzhen Composite Index stumbled 72.65 points or 3.64 percent to end at 1,924.90.

The lead from Wall Street is brutal as the major averages opened flat on Friday but quickly headed sharply lower, accelerating deeper into the red throughout the day to end at session lows.

The Dow plunged 949.73 points or 1.93 percent to finish at 48,147.33, while the NASDAQ plummeted 1,261.47 points or 5.28 percent to close at 22,617.73 and the S&P 500 tumbled 265.44 points or 3.70 percent to end at 6,910.39.

For the week, the NASDAQ nosedived by 10 percent, the S&P 500 plummeted by 8.6 percent and the Dow plunged by 8 percent.

The sell-off on Wall Street came amid continued weakness among technology stocks, as reflected by the steep drop by the tech-heavy NASDAQ. A steep drop by shares of Anthropic (ANT) weighed on the tech sector following its record-breaking initial public offering on Thursday.

Concerns about the outlook for interest rates also contributed to the selling pressure, with at least a quarter-point rate hike seen as a near-certainty at the Federal Reserve's monetary policy next month. Traders are increasingly worried the Fed will continue to raise rates in the coming months in order to combat stubborn inflation.

Crude oil prices moved higher on Friday as vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz continue to suffer attacks. West Texas Intermediate crude for December delivery was up by $0.72 or 0.87 percent at $83.93 per barrel.
